sentences.text: Sinosauropteryx was a small theropod dinosaur characterized by an unusually long tail and short arms.
The animal was covered in a coat of simple, filament-like feathers.
Preserved feather structures indicate that the dinosaur had a countershading body pattern and a banded tail.
However, the reddish-brown coloration previously attributed to this species was actually based on melanosomes found in a separate genus, Huadanosaurus.
The first fossil specimen of Sinosauropteryx prima was discovered in August 1996 by the farmer Li Yumin.
The species was first described by Ji and Ji in 1996.
A second species, S. lingyuanensis, was named by Qiu and colleagues in 2025.
Currently, only one species, S. prima, has been formally named, referring to its status as the first discovered non-avian feathered dinosaur species.
Specimen NIGP 127587 of Sinosauropteryx prima contained several small eggs in its abdomen alongside lizard remains.
The eggs preserved in this specimen measured 36 mm in length and 26 mm in width.
A specimen containing mammal jaws was later reclassified as a tyrannosauroid, casting doubt on whether Sinosauropteryx fed on venomous mammals.
Researchers John Ruben and colleagues suggested that a pigmented area on the holotype's abdomen represented the liver, part of a "hepatic piston" respiratory system similar to that of crocodiles.
While initially thought to belong to the family Compsognathidae with Compsognathus, later analyses placed Sinosauropteryx in its own family, Sinosauropterygidae.
A larger specimen previously assigned to S. prima, GMV 2124, was later reclassified as likely belonging to Tyrannosauroidea.
Three specimens have been described; the third specimen previously assigned to this genus represents either a second unnamed species or a distinct related genus.
Sinosauropteryx lived in northeastern China during the Early Cretaceous period.
The dinosaur is a member of the Jehol Biota, an assemblage of organisms found in the Yixian and Jiufotang Formations.
The climate during its time was temperate with distinct wet and dry seasons, averaging about 10 C yearly, which indicates unusually cold winters for the Mesozoic era.
Initial studies of the first Sinosauropteryx specimen concluded that the preserved structures were not modern feathers, though their exact nature remained uncertain.
Some researchers have suggested the filamentous impressions are collagen fibers rather than feathers, but this view is not widely accepted.
Some researchers proposed that the filamentous structures on Sinosauropteryx were collagen fibers forming a frill, rather than primitive feathers.
Most researchers rejected the hypothesis that the structures on Sinosauropteryx were collagen fibers.
